themes.label: Exams and grading
themes.selection: Check the current exam formats and assessment weights, and consider how the exam schedule fits with your other courses.
themes.study: Confirm the exam scope and format early. Practise under timed conditions and focus on understanding rather than memorising answers.

themes.label: Assignments and projects
themes.selection: Map assignments and projects across the semester before combining this course with other demanding courses.
themes.study: Break each task into milestones, prepare an early draft, and leave time for feedback and revisions.

themes.label: Reading, writing and presentations
themes.selection: If you are taking other courses with substantial reading or presentations, compare their deadlines before finalising your course combination.
themes.study: Note the arguments and evidence as you read. Outline essays and presentations first, then check clarity and citations.

evidence.quote: There are pre-readings and quiz each week.

sections.content: The content is mainly about different types of information systems, what problems they can address, and how managers should make decisions, along with many case studies.
sections.teaching: Great teaching. He is good at inspring students. Maybe the best teacher at UST. The class is quite engaging.
sections.grading: The exam is not difficult. It is not hard to pass the course, but getting A needs more efforts in writing reports and need to participate in the class more actively.
sections.workload: There are pre-readings and quiz each week. Two assignments. Sometimes presentations are needed.
